Text: A class is a {{c1::blueprint}}; an object is a {{c2::runtime instance}}.
Extra: Class/object distinction is the base of OOP. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: Constructors have {{c1::no return type}} and use the {{c2::class name}}.
Extra: A constructor is not a normal method. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/constructors.html

Text: Java generates a default constructor only when the class declares {{c1::no constructors}}.
Extra: Any explicit constructor disables generated no-arg constructor. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/constructors.html

Text: `this` refers to the {{c1::current object}}.
Extra: Useful when fields and parameters share names. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/thiskey.html

Text: `this(...)` must be the {{c1::first statement}} in a constructor.
Extra: Constructor chaining must happen before other statements. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/thiskey.html

Text: Java passes object arguments by {{c1::value}}, where the copied value is the {{c2::reference value}}.
Extra: This explains mutation vs reassignment behavior. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/arguments.html

Text: Encapsulation protects object {{c1::state}} behind a controlled {{c2::API}}.
Extra: Not just getters/setters. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/concepts/

Text: Fields should usually be {{c1::private}} by default.
Extra: Protect invariants and representation. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: A defensive copy protects internal mutable {{c1::reference}} state.
Extra: Avoid leaking mutable lists/arrays. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: Inheritance should model an {{c1::IS-A}} relationship.
Extra: Use composition for HAS-A. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/subclasses.html

Text: Java supports {{c1::single}} class inheritance.
Extra: A class can extend one direct superclass. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/subclasses.html

Text: Constructors are {{c1::not inherited}} by subclasses.
Extra: Subclass constructors call superclass constructors. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/subclasses.html

Text: Instance methods can be {{c1::overridden}}, while static methods are {{c2::hidden}}.
Extra: Fields are also hidden, not polymorphic. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/override.html

Text: An overriding method cannot be {{c1::more restrictive}} than the overridden method.
Extra: Preserves substitutability. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/override.html

Text: Overloading is resolved at {{c1::compile time}}.
Extra: Different parameter lists. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: Overriding is resolved at {{c1::runtime}} for instance methods.
Extra: Dynamic method dispatch. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: The reference type controls what the {{c1::compiler}} allows you to call.
Extra: Object type controls overridden method implementation. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: The actual object type controls which {{c1::overridden instance method}} runs.
Extra: This is runtime polymorphism. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: Upcasting is usually {{c1::implicit and safe}}.
Extra: Subclass to superclass. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: Downcasting is {{c1::explicit and risky}}.
Extra: May throw ClassCastException. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: `instanceof` helps prevent {{c1::ClassCastException}} before downcasting.
Extra: Pattern matching reduces repeated casts. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: Abstraction focuses on {{c1::what}} an object does, not {{c2::how}} it does it.
Extra: Hide implementation details. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/abstract.html

Text: An abstract class can have {{c1::instance fields}} and {{c2::constructors}}.
Extra: Interfaces cannot have instance fields or constructors. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/abstract.html

Text: Interface fields are implicitly {{c1::public static final}}.
Extra: They are constants. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/createinterface.html

Text: Interface abstract methods are implicitly {{c1::public abstract}}.
Extra: Default/static/private interface methods have special rules. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/createinterface.html

Text: Default methods were added to support interface {{c1::evolution}}.
Extra: They provide fallback implementation. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/defaultmethods.html

Text: A class can implement {{c1::multiple interfaces}}.
Extra: This supports multiple contracts/capabilities. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/createinterface.html

Text: Choose an interface for a {{c1::capability}} and an abstract class for shared {{c2::identity/state}}.
Extra: Practical design distinction. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/abstract.html

Text: Frequent downcasting can signal a weak {{c1::abstraction}}.
Extra: The common type may not expose needed behavior. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/polymorphism.html

Text: Composition models {{c1::HAS-A}}, while inheritance models {{c2::IS-A}}.
Extra: Prefer composition for reuse-only cases. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/subclasses.html

Text: Private interface methods were added in Java {{c1::9}}.
Extra: They share helper code inside interfaces. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/createinterface.html

Text: Default and static methods in interfaces arrived in Java {{c1::8}}.
Extra: API evolution feature. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/defaultmethods.html

Text: A subclass constructor must eventually call a {{c1::superclass constructor}}.
Extra: Explicitly or implicitly. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/constructors.html

Text: The `new` operator returns a {{c1::reference}} to the created object.
Extra: Oracle summary of object creation. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/objectcreation.html

Text: Object state lives in the {{c1::heap object}}, while local reference variables live in {{c2::stack frames}}.
Extra: Simplified memory model. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/objectcreation.html

Text: Public fields make internal representation part of the {{c1::public API}}.
Extra: Harder to change later. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: A method signature includes name and {{c1::parameter list}}, not return type alone.
Extra: Overloading rule. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/javaOO/index.html

Text: A private method is not overridden because the subclass cannot {{c1::see}} it.
Extra: Private members are class-local. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/override.html

Text: A final method cannot be {{c1::overridden}}.
Extra: It locks inherited behavior. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/override.html

Text: An interface name can be used anywhere a {{c1::type}} can be used.
Extra: Contract-based programming. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/createinterface.html
